To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we give an O(n /spl Theta/(d/sup 2/)) time exact algorithm for tree-based technology mapping for CLB with two independent LUTs, and we give an O (n/sup 3/), exact algorithm for tree based technology mapping for CLBS with several independent Luts.
we give an O(n /sup 3/) time algorithm for minimum area tree based technology mapping to CLBs with independent LUTS of two different sizes.
we have presented an exact algorithm for tree-based technology mapping onto ICLBs, and we have shown that the algorithm can also be applied to mapping onto CLBs with different ICLB configurations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) Given a tree network, how to find the optimal mapping to a class of ICLBs? and (2) How to combine the optimal solutions for several trees to obtain the optimal solution for a general network?
the following questions: (1) Given an n-node tree network and a target ICLB, what is the minimum number of ICLBs required to map the tree onto the ICLBs?
the exact mapping of logic networks onto FPGAs with ICLBs, which is a challenging problem due to the large number of possible configurations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have presented the first exact tree-based mapping algorithm for ICLBs.
the exact tree-based mapping problem for ICLBs is solved in O(n/sup d+2/) time, for a given tree with maximum indegree d.
the problem of mapping onto ICLBs is solved exactly in O(n/sup d+2/) time, where d is the indegree of any tree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a tree network, we have given the first O(n/sup d+2/)/spl Omega/(n) time exact mapping algorithm for ICLBs.
we have given the first exact algorithms for minimum area technology mapping onto ICLBs, and have improved the running time of the previous heuristic for tree networks by a factor of /spl Theta/n.

, we have developed an exact algorithm with running time O(n/sup d/), where d = O(1) for CLBs with two LUTs, O(n/sup logn/) for CLBs with three LUTs, and O(n/sup (d+1)/) for general CLBs with d independent LUTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a few additional constraints, the tree-based mapping problem can be solved exactly in polynomial time, and the solution can be extended to general networks with a small increase in run time.
the problem of tree-based technology mapping for ICLBs with two LUT sizes is solvable in polynomial time.
the problem of technology mapping onto CLBs with independent LUTS of two different sizes is NP-complete and can be solved optimally in polynomial time for a tree network.
